properties.areaDesc: Yukon Flats; White Mountains and High Terrain South of the Yukon River; Upper Chena River Valley
properties.headline: Winter Storm Warning issued October 19 at 5:58AM AKDT until October 21 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow expected. Total snow accumulations of 5 to 10
inches expected. Wind could gust as high as 35 mph across higher
elevations.

* WHERE...Upper Chena River Valley, Southern and Eastern Yukon Flats,
White Mountains, and Eagle Summit.

* WHEN...From 10 AM Tuesday to 4 PM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Gusty winds could lead to
areas of blowing snow which could reduce visibility below one half
mile at times.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...There will be a narrow snow gradient. The
highest potential for heaviest snow lies southeast of Fort Yukon.
West and north of there, the likelihood for heavier snow drops
quickly. Locations near Beaver and Livengood may end up getting
closer to 3 to 5 inches or less.
properties.instruction:
If you must travel, keep an extra flashlight, food, water, and warm
clothing in your vehicle in case of an emergency. Visit
511.alaska.gov or call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

properties.description:

inches expected, with 2 to 5 inches expected from Northway to the
Alcan Border along the Alaska Highway. Locally higher snow totals

Winds could gust as high as 35 mph. Rain may mix with snow in the

* WHEN...From 10 PM this evening to 4 PM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. Areas of blowing snow
could significantly reduce visibility.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Northwest wind gusts may be as high as 35 mph
Tuesday morning into early Wednesday morning.
properties.instruction:

clothing in your vehicle in case of an emergency. Visit
511.alaska.gov or call 5 1 1 for the latest road conditions.

properties.headline: Winter Storm Watch issued October 19 at 5:58AM AKDT until October 21 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow possible. Total snow accumulations of 4 to 8
inches possible.

* WHERE...Fairbanks North Star Borough and Nenana.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Wednesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
could impact the Tuesday evening and Wednesday morning commutes.

inches or less. A 30 mile change east or west will result in
drastic differences.

properties.areaDesc: Lake, FL; Volusia, FL
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 19 at 9:56AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds have caused river levels on the St Johns
at Astor to rise into Moderate Flood Stage this morning. The river is
forecast to climb slowly through Moderate Flood Stage through the end
of this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.0 feet, Water approaches or may enter lowest homes
on or near Wildhog Road and nearby canals. Flooding reaches the
parking lot of the Juno Trail Apartments. Flooding on portions of
Alligator Road and Holiday Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue
Creek are flooded. Roads at Astor Landing Campground and Lake
Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood. Water enters lower homes closest
to the river on McPherson Lane.

At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on or near
Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several inches of
water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at Astor Bridge
marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged. Bartram Rd and
Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards completely submerged.
Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded in South Moon Fish Camp,
docks and yards at condominiums on Juno Trail and water breaches the
sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Monday the stage was 3.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Monday was 3.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 3.1 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1115 PM EDT.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Flagler; Northeast Coastal St. Johns; Southeast Coastal St. Johns
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 19 at 9:56AM EDT until October 22 at 4:00AM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding.
For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 7 to 10 feet.
For the High Rip Current Risk, dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Flagler, Northeast Coastal St. Johns and
Southeast Coastal St. Johns Counties.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 AM EDT
Thursday. For the High Surf Advisory, until 8 PM EDT Tuesday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected. Dangerous swimming and
surfing conditions and localized beach erosion. Rip currents
can sweep even the best swimmers away from shore into deeper
water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: Eureka / Tahneta Pass; Western Copper Valley
properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued October 19 at 5:22AM AKDT until October 21 at 4:00AM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Snow expected. Total snow accumulations between 6 and 12
inches. Highest amounts between Eureka and Sheep Mountain.

* WHERE...Eureka / Tahneta Pass and Western Copper Valley.

* WHEN...From 10 PM this evening to 4 AM AKDT Wednesday.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be difficult. Be prepared for slippery
roads.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Occasional light snow today will give way to
steadier snowfall this evening through Tuesday evening before
slowly tapering off by Wednesday morning. The heaviest snow is
expected to fall between early Tuesday morning and Tuesday evening.
